appraisal_events.evidence: « combien d'intelligence et de goût latent s'étaient brusquement développés en elle depuis Balbec » ; « Quel changement depuis Balbec où je défie Elstir lui-même d'avoir pu deviner en Albertine ces richesses de poésie » ; qualified by « Je trouvais que c'était un peu trop bien dit », « une poésie moins étrange, moins personnelle que celle de Céleste Albaret » and « elle est mon œuvre ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Albertine is given a long virtuosic set-piece on ices that the narrator admits he could never have produced himself, which locally raises her as a speaker of unexpected imaginative power. The elevation is real but ironized: the narrator hedges the praise, ranks her poetry below Céleste's, and immediately annexes her gift as his own creation and as proof of his hold over her.

appraisal_events.evidence: « je sentis quelle fatigue était pour moi cette présence perpétuelle » ; « si, par une même ingéniosité, la conteuse persane retardait sa mort, je hâtais la mienne » ; the covert interrogation of the chauffeur about Versailles ; « savaient parfaitement, pendant que j'étais amoureux de Gilberte, que j'étais dupe » ; « mon amour-propre blessé ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator narrates himself into exhaustion, jealous surveillance and humiliation: he must invent daily pretexts like a Scheherazade who hastens rather than delays her own death, spies on Albertine through the chauffeur while fearing that spying would be humiliating for him, and learns from Gilberte's former maid that he was known to be a dupe by people who despised him.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine dominates the passage's speech, sustaining an elaborate figurative rhapsody that the narrator concedes he could not have spoken and that he judges to have made her unrecognizable since Balbec.

She gains relative leverage: the narrator is worn down, jealous and dependent on stratagems and chaperones, and the narration discloses that she quietly managed the chauffeur while the narrator suspected nothing.
His dominant local condition is anxious surveillance, physical fatigue, and doubled jealousy, capped by the retrospective discovery of his own duped position with Gilberte.
The passage exposes him as a jailer and dupe whose self-flattering claims of power over Albertine are undercut by the very narration that reports them.
In the comparison that qualifies Albertine's brilliance, Céleste is placed above her as the source of a stranger, more personal poetry Albertine could never have found.

ambiguities: The narrator's appraisal of Albertine's speech is genuinely double: he is « profondément attendri » and defies Elstir to have foreseen such poetry, yet in the same breath calls it « un peu trop bien dit », of « grâce assez facile », and inferior to Céleste's — and he attributes it to his own influence (« elle est mon œuvre »). The local elevation stands, but whether the passage endorses or ironizes it is underdetermined.

The chauffeur episode is staged with explicit dramatic irony: the narrator declares his confidence complete and finds Albertine innocent, while the narration adds « Comment aurais-je supposé que cette rectification… venait de ce qu'… Albertine, alarmée que le chauffeur m'eût parlé, s'était soumise, avait fait la paix avec lui. » It is therefore unstable whether Albertine is locally cleared or has covertly outmaneuvered both men.
